neighbours.label: ' feels' / 'comes off as' giving a critic's impression of a work in a review (it feels forced; comes across as ...); the top examples also include the opening quote of a string argument in code
fire: The first season was sharp and funny, but the new one feels tired and overlong.
The lead actor tries hard, yet every big speech comes off as rehearsed and hollow.
The level design is clever, but by the final world the platforming feels like busywork.
For all its expensive sets, the film feels strangely small and airless.
The memoir has some lovely passages, though the second half feels rushed to meet a deadline.
The restaurant's new menu is ambitious, but the tasting course comes across as fussy.
The remake copies every scene of the original, and the result feels lifeless.
The novel's villain is meant to be frightening, but he comes off as a cartoon.
quiet: The first season was sharp and funny, but the new one was cancelled after six episodes.
The lead actor trained hard, and every big speech was recorded in a single take.
The wool blanket feels warm and heavy on a cold night in the cabin.
For all its expensive sets, the film was shot in only thirty days.
The nurse asked whether the bandage feels too tight around the ankle.
The restaurant's new menu is ambitious, and the tasting course costs ninety dollars.
The remake copies every scene of the original, and it opened in March.
The novel's villain is a banker who runs across the border with the money.

notes: Card: ' feels' x4 and ' as' (comes across as) in reviews, mixed with opening string quotes in Python calls. Probes: review 'feels like a chore' 0.55, 'feels cheap' 0.35, 'comes off as desperate' 0.72; tactile 'feels soft' 0.03, 'how the knee feels' 0.09. Weak pole (max 6.2). Only the review sense is tested here; the code-quote part is not.
